question: Should OpenClaw adopt a general externally managed config ownership mode and make it the maintained Kubernetes default?
rationale: This introduces a new environment-level ownership contract and changes mutation, recovery, reload, and maintained deployment behavior across stable surfaces; repository evidence supports the direction but cannot establish maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt managed ownership
options.body: Define a general immutable external-config contract and use it in the maintained Kubernetes manifests with focused upgrade and live-cluster proof.

options.title: Keep rollout reconciliation
options.body: Retain copied mutable config and deployment restarts, limiting work to reload-baseline correctness and clearer operator diagnostics.

recommendation.title: Adopt managed ownership
recommendation.body: Define a general immutable external-config contract and use it in the maintained Kubernetes manifests with focused upgrade and live-cluster proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The hot-reload behavior and recent runtime-state refactors trace directly to this owner, who also opened the product-direction issue.
